item.subject: science
item.chapter_label: The night sky: Moon and calendars
item.stem:
Dev sketches the Moon on five nights and sees the bright part change shape.

What is changing?

options.A: The Moon itself is swelling and shrinking, because phase is another word for size.
options.B: The bright part we see from Earth changes, even though the Moon does not emit its own light.
options.C: Earth sees only the night side, so the bright part we see is the Moon's unlit half.
options.D: The rule holds even if we drop the fact that the Moon does not shine by itself.

followup.stem: Assign oxidation numbers first. The species is [[1]] if OS increases, [[2]] if OS decreases, or [[3]] if OS stays the same.
followup.why: A mixture with uniform composition throughout is homogeneous; a mixture that is not uniform, has visible particles, or settles with time is heterogeneous. This is the hinge move, not a reprint of the clicked option.
